details.description: gpt-oss-safeguard-120b is OpenAI's open-weight reasoning model for safety classification, released as a research preview in October 2025 under an Apache 2.0 license. It is a reasoning fine-tune of gpt-oss-120b (117 billion total / 5.1 billion active parameters) that takes a user-supplied written policy and a piece of content, classifies the content against that policy, and returns its chain-of-thought reasoning alongside the decision rather than only a score. It supports low, medium and high reasoning-effort settings and, like the base gpt-oss models, requires OpenAI's harmony response format. OpenAI recommends the base gpt-oss models for non-safety use cases.
advantages: OpenAI reports that on internal multi-policy accuracy tests, gpt-oss-safeguard-120b outperforms gpt-5-thinking and the base gpt-oss models, per OpenAI's launch post.
OpenAI reports gpt-oss-safeguard slightly outperformed all other tested models on a 2022 content-moderation dataset, per OpenAI's launch post.
Exposes its reasoning process for each classification decision, making it possible to audit why content was labeled a certain way, per OpenAI's Hugging Face model card.
Interprets a custom, written policy at inference time rather than requiring retraining, so one model can generalize across products and use cases, per OpenAI's launch post.
disadvantages: Released as a research preview, per OpenAI's launch post.
Performance was mixed on the ToxicChat benchmark, where gpt-5-thinking marginally outperformed gpt-oss-safeguard-120b, per OpenAI's launch post.

OpenAI notes traditional classifiers trained on large labeled datasets can still outperform gpt-oss-safeguard, and its reasoning process is more computationally expensive to run at scale, per OpenAI's launch post.
Requires OpenAI's harmony response format; OpenAI recommends the base gpt-oss models for applications outside safety classification, per OpenAI's Hugging Face model card.
use_cases: LLM input/output filtering against a custom safety policy
Offline Trust and Safety labeling at scale
Auditable, policy-based content classification where explainability matters more than speed

notes: No exact numeric benchmark scores were published by OpenAI for gpt-oss-safeguard-120b (only comparative statements like 'outperforms gpt-5-thinking'), so evaluations is left empty rather than guess. Catalog facts list two max_input_tokens values (128000, 131072) and two max_output_tokens values (16000, 131072) depending on host; sources gave no single context/output figure for this model, so no specific number is stated in the description. Exact release day not independently confirmed beyond 'October 2025'.
